title: The 10 Best Soldering Irons
subtitle: Soldering irons, stations and guns for electronics and wiring, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: We ranked 10 corded best-sellers, from $10 pencil-iron kits to Hakko and Weller stations, on rating, review volume and features (temperature control, a display, auto sleep, spare tips and a ready-to-use kit). Most picks are aimed at electronics; the Weller gun is for heavy wire and stained glass.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

products.name: YIHUA 926 III 60W Digital Display Soldering Iron Station Kit with 2 Helping Hands, 6 Extra Tips, Lead-Free Solder
products.best_for: Hobbyists who solder often and want a proper station without spending $100+.
products.verdict: A compact digital station with a built-in iron holder, adjustable sleep mode (5, 10 or 30 minutes), temperature calibration and a full set of accessories including two helping hands.
cons: 60 W is modest for heavy wire

specs.included: Station, iron, 6 tips (900M series), 2 helping hands, lead-free solder, solder sucker, tweezers

products.name: Liouhoum 80W LCD Digital Soldering Iron Kit, Adjustable Temperature, Fast Heat-Up
products.best_for: First-time solderers and occasional repairs on a tight budget.
products.verdict: The best-selling iron in the search: an 80 W plug-in pencil iron with an LCD temperature readout, a 5-minute auto sleep on the stand and temperature memory, sold as a kit for about $10.

products.name: YIHUA 939D+ Digital Soldering Station, 75W Equivalent, Built-in Transformer, ESD Safe
products.best_for: Regular solderers who want a sturdier station than the 926 III.
products.verdict: A transformer-based station with a brushed aluminum panel, three temperature memories, sleep and auto shutdown, and a detachable 907F iron. YIHUA pitches it at people who solder regularly.

products.name: HANDSKIT 90W Soldering Iron Kit for Electronics, Adjustable Temp 180-480°C, 21-in-1
products.best_for: DIYers who want a full kit with a carrying case.
products.verdict: A 90 W digital pencil iron with temperature calibration, 15-minute auto sleep, temperature memory and six 900M tips, packed in a case with a desoldering pump and magnifier.

specs.included: Iron, 6 900M tips, stand, desoldering pump, magnifier, solder, tweezers, case

products.name: Weller 70 Watt Digital Soldering Station WE1010NA
products.best_for: Shops and classrooms that want a name-brand station with locked settings.
products.verdict: Weller's digital station holds temperature within plus or minus 4°F, with standby, auto setback, a temperature lock and password protection, and a silicone cable on the 70 W iron.

specs.included: Station, WEP70 iron, PH70 safety rest with sponge, ETA 1.6 mm screwdriver tip

products.name: Q-MING 60W Soldering Iron Kit with 5 Interchangeable Tips, 10-in-1 Adjustable Temperature
products.best_for: Beginners who want a no-frills kit with the basics.
products.verdict: A simple 60 W pencil iron with a temperature dial and a ceramic heater, packed with five tips, fine 0.6 mm solder and flux.

specs.included: Iron, stand, sponge, 5 tips, 0.6 mm solder, flux

products.name: PINECIL Smart Mini Portable Soldering Iron
products.best_for: Makers who want a small, fast iron for the bench or the road.
products.verdict: A pocket-size smart iron with a RISC-V chip and a screen, powered by a USB-C PD/QC charger or a DC barrel jack. It reaches working temperature in 12 seconds and drops into standby when idle.

specs.included: Iron, B2 tip (power supply not included)

products.name: Weller 260W/200W Professional Soldering Gun Kit with Three Tips and Solder in Carrying Case
products.best_for: Heavy wire, cable lugs, stained glass and other jobs that soak up heat.
products.verdict: A heavy-duty dual-heat soldering gun that reaches 900-1100°F in 6 seconds, with the trigger selecting high or low power. It's for heavy wire, stained glass and sheet metal, not circuit boards.

specs.included: Gun, 3 tips (incl. smoothing tip), solder, carrying case

products.name: Hakko FX888DX-010 Digital Soldering Station with Rotary Encoder
products.best_for: Serious hobbyists and pros who want a proven Hakko station.
products.verdict: Hakko's updated FX-888D with a rotary encoder for setting the temperature and a 50-480°C range. It's the best-rated station on this list at 4.8 stars.

specs.included: Station, iron, holder, sponge, tip cleaner, T18-D16 chisel tip

products.name: Hakko FX601-02 Adjustable Temperature Controlled Soldering Iron, 67 Watts
products.best_for: People who want Hakko-quality temperature control without a base station.
products.verdict: A plug-in Hakko pencil iron with closed-loop temperature control: a sensor in the heater keeps the tip at the temperature you dial in, with a lock key to fix the setting.

avoid.name: 300W High Power Soldering Iron Kit 110V, Industrial Grade External Heating Soldering Iron with Replacement Tip, Heating Core and Stand
avoid.verdict: A 300 W iron with no temperature control, sold for circuit repair, with a spec table that rates it to only 480°F.
reasons: The bullets list circuit repair among its uses, but nothing in the listing mentions adjustable or controlled temperature. An uncontrolled 300 W iron on a circuit board lifts pads and cooks components.
The spec table gives an upper temperature of 480°F, which contradicts the 'industrial grade' 300 W pitch and sits barely above the roughly 423°F melting point of common lead-free solder.
For heavy work, the Weller D550PK gun heats in 6 seconds and has a lifetime warranty; for electronics, any temperature-controlled iron on this list is the right tool.

buyers_guide.a: A pencil iron plugs straight into the wall and is fine for occasional repairs. A station puts the controls in a separate base, holds temperature better under load, and usually has a proper holder. A soldering gun is for heavy wire, lugs and stained glass, and is too hot for circuit boards.

buyers_guide.q: How many watts do I need?
buyers_guide.a: For electronics, 60-80 W with temperature control is plenty. More watts mostly means faster recovery when the tip touches a big joint. High wattage without temperature control is a liability on boards.

buyers_guide.q: What temperature should I solder at?
buyers_guide.a: Leaded 60/40 solder melts at about 370°F (188°C) and is usually worked around 600-650°F. Lead-free solder melts around 423°F (217°C) and usually needs 650-700°F. Go hotter only for large joints.
Yes, if you leave the iron on between jobs. Dropping the temperature when idle slows oxidation and makes tips last much longer, and it's a safety net if you forget to switch off.

buyers_guide.q: What does the Pinecil need to run?
buyers_guide.a: A USB-C charger that supports PD or QC 3.0, or a DC barrel supply. None is in the box, and a weak phone charger won't give it full power.
Spare tips fit only their own series (900M, T18, T19 and so on). Check what's included and what replacement tips cost before you buy, because tips wear out.
